title: From Chai Pani to Cal-India Collective: Indian Chefs Storm the James Beard Awards 2026
excerpt: Multiple Indian-origin chefs and restaurants earn nominations at America's most prestigious culinary honour, with winners to be announced on June 15 in Chicago.
body:
The James Beard Awards — often called the Oscars of the American food world — have become an unlikely stage for India's culinary diaspora. In 2026, several Indian-origin chefs and restaurants earned nominations across multiple categories, marking one of the strongest showings for South Asian cuisine in the awards' four-decade history.

## A California Collective Takes Centre Stage

Srijith Gopinathan and Ayesha Thapar, co-leaders of Cal-India Collective, are competing for the National Outstanding Restaurateur award. Their hospitality group operates a portfolio of acclaimed restaurants — Ettan, Copra, Eylan, and Little Blue Door — spread across Palo Alto, San Francisco, Menlo Park, and Los Altos, California. Each restaurant explores a different facet of Indian culinary traditions, reimagined through California's farm-to-table ethos.

Their nomination comes alongside Meherwan Irani and Molly Irani of the Chai Pani Restaurant Group, who are also in the running for the same award. Chai Pani, their Asheville, North Carolina, flagship, won the Outstanding Restaurant award in 2022 for its vibrant rendition of Indian street food and chaat. Their fast-casual concept Botiwalla has since expanded to multiple locations across the South.

## New Names, Historic Firsts

The 2026 nominations include several other noteworthy entries. Tamba, a contemporary Indian restaurant in Town Square, Las Vegas, earned a spot in the Best New Restaurant category. The restaurant has drawn attention for its live-fire cooking techniques, coastal dishes, and modern presentation of traditional Indian recipes.

Perhaps the most remarkable story belongs to Chef Suresh Sundas of Daru, who became the first-ever Nepalese chef to be named a James Beard Award finalist, earning recognition in the Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic category. Sundas, who never attended culinary school, learned to cook at his family home in southeastern Nepal — a trajectory that underscores how deeply personal heritage shapes South Asian culinary excellence in America.

## A Pattern, Not an Anomaly

The 2026 nominations sit within a broader wave. Tresind Studio in Dubai recently became the first Indian restaurant anywhere to hold three Michelin stars. Vijay Kumar of Semma won the 2025 James Beard Award for Best Chef: New York State. And La Liste's 2026 edition featured fourteen Indian restaurants, up from six in 2022.

Meanwhile, the inaugural Global Indian Restaurant Awards, held in London in June 2026, brought together 250 restaurateurs from across the world, with luminaries like two-time Michelin-starred chef Atul Kochhar and Vivek Singh of the Cinnamon Collection leading conference sessions on scaling culinary brands globally.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For the 5.5 million Indian-Americans watching from home, these nominations are more than professional accolades. They represent a shift in how Indian food is perceived in America — not as a takeout category but as a serious fine-dining tradition. The chefs being honoured are not simplifying Indian flavours for Western palates; they are deepening them.

The winners will be announced on June 15, 2026, at the Lyric Opera of Chicago. Whatever the outcome, the shortlist itself tells a story: Indian cuisine in America is no longer knocking on the door. It is setting the table.
author: Diaspora Desk
